subdomains.business_boundary: Pharmaceutical, biotechnology, and academic structural biology organizations need atomic-level models of proteins and nucleic acids and their dynamics to drive drug discovery, protein engineering, and mechanism elucidation. The subdomain covers professional workflows that produce, validate, or use atomic-resolution structure information such as X-ray and cryo-EM maps, PDB/EMDB depositions, molecular dynamics trajectories, docking poses, and predicted models. It is distinct from genomics (sequence-level data and interpretation), cell_imaging (cells and tissues at light-microscope resolution), and systems_microbial (organism and network-level behavior).
subdomains.occupations: Structural biologist; X-ray crystallographer; cryo-EM specialist; computational chemist; molecular modeler; structural bioinformatician; structure-based drug discovery scientist; protein engineer
subdomains.boundary_note: Boundary drawn at the molecular/atomic structure level: professionals produce, model or use atomic structures and molecular dynamics (PDB/EMDB models, trajectories, docking). All five candidates operate on molecular structure or dynamics data; anything sequence-only (genomics), cell or tissue imaging (cell_imaging), or organism and population modeling (systems_microbial) was excluded.

subdomains.business_boundary: Biomedical research institutions, pharmaceutical discovery and screening groups, clinical research and diagnostic laboratories, and institutional microscopy and cytometry core facilities need this subdomain's work done. It covers the quantitative measurement and interpretation of cells, tissues and subcellular structures by light and fluorescence microscopy and flow cytometry, plus the management, annotation, QC and sharing of the resulting image and cytometry data. It is separated from biomolecular (atomic-resolution structures and PDB/EMDB models) by its cellular-scale objects, from genomics (sequence and expression data) by image-based measurement, and from systems_microbial (organism-, microbial-population- and network-level modeling) by its single-cell and tissue observational unit.
subdomains.occupations: Flow cytometry specialist; imaging scientist; microscopy core facility custodian; high-content screening scientist; bioimage analyst; cell biologist; image data steward; histology and tissue-imaging specialist; research microscopist
subdomains.boundary_note: Boundary drawn at cellular and tissue-scale measurement via microscopy and cytometry plus the metadata, QC and data stewardship around those measurements. All four candidates sit inside that boundary: a cytometry reporting standard, an instrument QC program, a morphological profiling assay, and public image-archive deposition. Atomic structure work (biomolecular) and sequence analysis (genomics) were excluded.

subdomains.business_boundary: Genomics work is commissioned by clinical diagnostic laboratories, biopharma research units, agricultural and conservation breeding programs, and university or private sequencing core facilities. Its object is sequence-level evidence: assemblies, variant calls, expression measurements, and their quality certificates, produced from sequencing-instrument outputs (Illumina, PacBio, ONT). It is separated from biomolecular (atomic-structure-level work) because its outputs are sequences, not structures; from cell_imaging because its evidence is reads and counts rather than images; from systems_microbial because it stops at a single genome or transcriptome rather than modelling whole organisms, communities, or regulatory networks.
subdomains.occupations: Clinical molecular geneticist; molecular genetic pathologist; variant curation scientist; bioinformatics scientist (genomics); genome assembly specialist; NGS data analyst; sequencing core facility scientist
subdomains.boundary_note: Boundary drawn at sequence-level analysis of DNA and RNA, including clinical variant interpretation, expression quantification, genome assembly assessment and truth-set benchmarking. All four candidates are sequence-analysis workflows ending in interpretation or benchmark reports; structural and molecular modeling (biomolecular), microscopy (cell_imaging), and organismal network modeling (systems_microbial) were excluded.

subdomains.business_boundary: Clinical microbiology laboratories, public-health and infection-control institutions, antimicrobial stewardship programs, systems-biology research groups, microbiome research programs and industrial biotechnology need this work: susceptibility testing of clinical isolates with breakpoint interpretation, genome-scale and kinetic metabolic modeling, curation of computable models, and microbial-community (microbiome) data analysis and reporting. Separated from biomolecular (structure-level objects), genomics (raw sequence analysis, though microbiome analysis consumes sequences) and cell_imaging (cell/tissue measurement) by its organism-, population- and network-level objects.
subdomains.occupations: Clinical microbiologist; medical laboratory scientist; antimicrobial stewardship pharmacist; systems biologist; metabolic modeler; computational microbiologist; microbiome bioinformatician; microbial ecologist; industrial biotechnologist
subdomains.boundary_note: Boundary drawn at organism-, population- and network-level objects of microbial and systems biology: antimicrobial susceptibility testing of clinical isolates with breakpoint interpretation (EUCAST), genome-scale metabolic reconstruction (Thiele-Palsson protocol with MEMOTE quality assurance), curation of computable models (BioModels with MIRIAM annotation), reproducible microbiome community analysis (QIIME 2) and human microbiome study reporting (STORMS). Every candidate's primary object is a microbial population, a metabolic network or a community-level dataset, not a single molecule (biomolecular), not sequence analysis per se (genomics) and not cell or tissue morphology measurement (cell_imaging). The S1-01-moved Gillespie gene-regulatory-network simulation task is treated as adjacent, simulation rather than curation or reconstruction, and is not overruled.
